atomic_claims.text: The frozen eight-vertex graph has a representation by two disjoint filled simple polygons with 28 and 8 corners; all eighteen graph edges avoid them and all ten nonedges have strict interior hits. Exact obstacle number one versus two is not decided.

Complete complement-degree enumeration through orders five to eight, checked isomorphism orbits and separator/Kuratowski/rotation certificates leave one non-bipyramid four-connected maximal planar graph at order eight and none below it.

The full necessary guarded CNF has 156 variables, 31676 clauses and all 1502 simple paths; the exhibited real direction table admits exactly two of 1024 labelings. This is a SAT witness, not exhaustive realizable-order-type classification.

For any finite graph and any matching of q nonedges, some rational GP placement admits one free square hitting all q selected pairs. Other nonedges need not be blocked. Hence a fixed target set containing a three-edge nonedge matching cannot obey capacity two at every unrestricted placement.

The five targets fixed before screening are 02,14,27,36,57. The complete two-polygon witness has targets 14,27,36 in the same interior obstacle, contradicting the proposed capacity-two property for this graph and target set.
